note: Track intervals, step 3 (ladder interval-ears:3): the major 2nd and the perfect 4th, tapped on the staff, then the ear game at the level before (the 3rds, the 5th and the octave) and at the game's own level 3, which adds the two. Each game's answers are named as its buttons show them with the plain word beside each, and every section has a feel to reach. Missing: a level word for interval-ears level 3 ("beginner" is 2, "intermediate" is 4), so the number is written.

exercise.title: The 2nd and the 4th by ear
exercise.why: A major 2nd is one step of the major scale and a perfect 4th is three, so humming up the scale from the low note to the high one tells you which of them you heard.

cells.text:
Tap {{1}}, then {{2}} on the staff below: a major 2nd, one step of the scale. Then tap {{1}}, then {{4}}: a perfect 4th, three steps up.
Practice until you can hum the top note of each before you tap it.

Press Start in the game below: it plays two notes, one after the other, and you pick the interval: m3 for a minor 3rd, M3 for a major 3rd, P5 for a 5th or P8 for an octave.
Press Replay to hear the two notes again before you pick.
Practice until the four answers come without humming.

Press Start in the game below. This round also asks M2 for a major 2nd and P4 for a perfect 4th.
When two answers sound alike, hum up the scale from the low note and count the steps.
Practice until the 4th and the 5th no longer get mixed up.
